subject: ventures/cake-pricing-calculator
professional: a custom-cake business owner / bakery pricing consultant (food-cost and labor-costing practice), checking first that labor, delivery and fees reach the price and that the quote check does not flatter a losing quote

evidence.correctness: Ran `node --test '*.test.mjs'` in ventures/cake-pricing-calculator: 22 pass, 0 fail. Recomputed three cases independently in Python with exact Fractions (not the author's tests): (1) sampleInput: materials 65.40, labor 130, delivery 24.38, overhead 15.632, cost 235.412, price 305.73, 12.74/serving, quoted $120 -> net 116.40, profit -119.01, take-home/hour 3.58, all matching node output; (2) servings 10, fee 10, margin 20 -> 107.14; (3) 40-serving wedding-size cake (fee 2.9, margin 35, quoted 500) -> price 1043.64, matching node. Price = cost/(1-fee-margin) is the standard margin-on-price formula.
evidence.completeness: Checked each README claim by running priceCake: materials, labor, delivery, overhead, fee and margin taken from price, three tiers, 50% deposit, quoted-price check, CSV export, example loader, usage opt-out. All work end to end (calc.mjs, index.html wiring, page.test.mjs). Stated not-modelled list is honest. No TODOs or stubs found. Deposit is a fixed 50% with no input.
evidence.verification: 22 tests pass (calc 9, page, usage). Seeded mutation: in calc.mjs changed the price divisor from (1 - (fee+margin)/100) to (1 - fee/100); 1 test failed ('fee and margin come out of the price, not on top of cost'), file reverted with git checkout, git status clean. Gaps: break-even/premium tier values are only asserted as ordered, not numerically; deposit value and the perHour formula with overhead are not independently asserted.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs, calc.test.mjs, index.html, usage.mjs. Small pure ES module, clear input validation and an error return, no dead code. Defects: num() strips '%', '$', ',' silently, so '1,5' becomes 15; wage interpolated into advice text unformatted (`$${v.wage}/hour`); overhead is charged on the baker's own labor, which is a debatable base; sitemap.xml, robots.txt Sitemap and canonical use relative URLs ('./index.html'), which crawlers do not accept.
evidence.claims: Backed: no-upload and no-account claim (index.html runs from local modules, usage stored locally with DNT/GPC honoured, usage.mjs and usage.test.mjs); disclaimer and no-warranty clause present in index.html footer and README; not-modelled list matches code. Not backed or wrong: llms.txt links the tool at https://duncan-haywood.github.io/oss-monorepo/cake-pricing-calculator/ (retired host) while README and VENTURE.yaml say https://marisstella.app/cake-pricing-calculator/; the FAQ line 'tripling $40 pays less than $15 an hour' is an illustration with no source; README's 'which used to leave a six-hour fondant cake paying less than minimum wage' is an unsourced anecdote. No fake reviews found.
evidence.fitness: Walked a baker's job: type a 24-serving cake with 6.5 h and a delivery, get 305.73 total and tiers 242.69/305.73/351.36, load a $120 past quote and see it lost $119.01 at $3.58/h. A baker can finish this in minutes and the output is actionable. Missing for real quoting: no tiered-cake handling, no rush/weekend surcharge, no sales tax, no market comparison, deposit not adjustable, no saved presets.
evidence.domain: Compared with standard food-cost/job-costing practice: labor at a stated wage, materials by serving, mileage plus drive time, and margin on price rather than markup are all correct and the wage-versus-profit separation is what a consultant wants. Departures: no allocation of oven/equipment time or fixed monthly overhead (a flat percent of materials+labor only), no waste or yield factor on ingredients, no tasting or revision time default, and no sales tax or payment-processor fixed fee (e.g. $0.30) beyond a percent fee. Would pass as a quote sanity-check, not as a pricing system.

defects.what: llms.txt points the tool at the retired github.io host instead of marisstella.app, so LLM crawlers get a stale URL
sitemap.xml, robots.txt Sitemap line and canonical link use relative URLs ('./index.html'); sitemap protocol requires absolute URLs, so SEO files do nothing
Fee is percent only; no fixed per-transaction fee, no sales tax, no ingredient waste or yield factor, deposit fixed at 50%
num() strips commas so a European decimal '1,5' is read as 15 without warning
Tests do not assert tier prices, deposit, or the quoted perHour with overhead and mileage non-zero; a mutation there would survive
Unsourced anecdote and FAQ illustration presented as fact

verdict: A small, correct, finished calculator: all recomputed outputs matched exactly and the one seeded mutation (dropping the margin from the price divisor) was caught by a test. A bakery pricing consultant would accept the method as a quote sanity check but would miss fixed processor fees, sales tax, waste and equipment time. Claims score 2 because llms.txt names a retired host and the sitemap/robots/canonical files use relative URLs, so the discoverability claims are not backed by working files. Under the computed rule it fails the bar on claims, but is finished.
